A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CBM-HNMU and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Reordered appendix sections and renumbered figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments, intervention ablations, visual masking and concept-replacement results, and a study involving 30 participants.

after.justification: V3 retains original classification experiments, supplementary intervention analyses, and the 30-participant user study.

M1.justification: The concept extraction, CLIP alignment, local CBM approximation, gradient-based concept selection, pruning, optional replacement, and reverse distillation procedures remain. Section 3.5 revises their mathematical specification without establishing a different implemented algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Flower-102, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and FGVC-Aircraft. The user-study population, masking scenarios, and appendix case-study coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the original black-box models, CBM, Post-hoc CBM, and random concept intervention. Tables 4 and 5 contain the same comparator sets.

E3.justification: The user-study description changes clustering into ten groups from per confused class to per confused-class pair, and redescribes CR as a shared semantic cue. These revise the reported protocol; the unchanged questionnaire and scores do not establish that the study was rerun. Model-training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Confused-class sensitivity, random intervention, concept replacement, approximation checks, non-intervened-class analysis, masking, and all nine appendix examples remain. Removing the main-text masking summary does not remove the analysis, which survives in v3 Appendix C.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain averages and standard deviations over three random tests. The user-study figures retain participant-based mean/standard-deviation reporting, and the supplementary statistical displays introduce no new estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Matched tables, user-study scores, and detailed appendix results are unchanged. However, removing v1 Figure 3 removes its inconsistent original bird-confidence value of 0; the detailed masking figure reports 1.90% before and 2.40% after masking in both versions. This is a limited reporting change, not evidence of improved experimental performance.

T1.justification: Section 3.5 rewrites Equation 6 using class-specific weight vectors and corrects Equation 7's vector products to explicit element-wise multiplication. Conversely, the predicted-class definition changes from arg max to max, introducing an index/value error. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about interpretable approximation, automatic intervention beyond individual samples, and annotation-free concept communication. The headline accuracy improvements of 2.64% and 1.03% are unchanged.

C2.justification: The user-study discussion now interprets CR as a cue shared by both classes and uses it with CT/CF agreement to argue that the same hints mislead humans and networks. This differs from v1's semantic-rationality/error-correlation framing and conflicts with the unchanged questionnaire's discriminative-helpfulness question. The limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The hardware, software environment, learning rates, epoch counts, distillation temperatures, intervention-count guidance, and code-access information are retained. The hardware and parameter appendices are relocated rather than expanded.

R1.justification: Section 3.5 drops the explicit attribution of the gradient intervention function to Interactive Concept Bottleneck Models [4] and A Closer Look at the Intervention Procedure of Concept Bottleneck Models [32], although both bibliography entries remain. The broader related-work discussion is unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites Section 3.5, the experimental overview, and the user-study discussion, and retitles Algorithm 1. The visualization appendix moves from A to H, with corresponding heading and reference updates; the main section structure and most prose remain.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is extensively revised: Figure 1 gains a worked example, the intervention and replacement diagrams are redrawn, appendix visualizations receive a consistent new design, and plots and tables are restyled or relocated. The redundant main masking summary disappears, and the user-study figure changes from full-width to single-column.

improvement.justification: The worked overview in Figure 1 and explicit element-wise contribution formulas improve explanation while preserving the empirical evidence. However, v3 introduces the max/arg max error and describes CR inconsistently with the unchanged questionnaire. These concrete gains and accuracy problems leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
